description: A document-store adapter the rest of the app depends on through an interface, plus an in-memory fake for tests. Acquires a token with the app's own credentials — not the signed-in user's — because the login flow keeps no user token: it requests only basic profile scope and discards the access token after reading the identity claims, so acting as the user would mean persisting and refreshing a per-user refresh token, a new secret at rest, to buy attribution that a recorded uploader field gives for free. Uploads small files in one request and larger ones through a resumable session; a pitch deck routinely exceeds the single-request ceiling, so the session path is not deferrable. Every credential the adapter handles — the client secret, the access token, and any signed URL it is given — must be unloggable, extending the existing redaction rather than adding a second mechanism.
expectedBehavior: Callers depend on an interface, not on the vendor SDK — the concrete client is constructed at the edge and injected
A fake implementation supports the whole interface, including forced failure, so the failure paths are testable without a tenant
Files above the single-request ceiling upload through a resumable session and arrive intact
No log line or error response contains the client secret, an access token, or a signed URL's signature parameter
A store failure surfaces as a typed error the caller can distinguish from a bad request
verificationSteps: Grep the diff for vendor SDK imports outside the adapter module and confirm there are none
Run an upload with logging at its most verbose, capture the output, and search it for the secret, the token and the signature parameter
